title: Desks, storage and cable management
intro: Coordinate desk surface, storage and cable routes around usable space, actual products, movement and service access.

sections.title: Calculate and define usable space
sections.text: Exercise only: a 1400 mm under-desk envelope with storage occupying 400 mm leaves ⁦1400 − 400 = 1000⁩ mm. This is geometric remainder, not proof of comfort or accessibility. Define measurement boundaries and check frame, base, chair and user movement.
sections.caption: 1000 mm is the geometric remainder only.

sections.title: Coordinate storage and movement
sections.text: Draw drawers open with the chair in use. Define contents, access and product-specific stability requirements. Fitting beneath the top does not prove freedom of movement. Test mobile storage in its actual working position, not a convenient display position.
sections.caption: Review storage with the chair and open drawers.

sections.title: Plan cable routing and access
sections.text: List devices, cable entries, supports and access covers. For moving or height-adjustable desks, check the documented route at travel limits under system instructions so cables are not pulled or trapped. Furniture details do not authorize electrical cable alterations; specialists review services while furniture provides coordinated routing and access.
sections.caption: Check the route through its movement states.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The 1000 mm remainder is correct, yet an open drawer obstructs the chair. Revise storage position and review access and cables, then repeat the task trial.
example.decision: Decision: complete the calculation with a movement check.

quiz.question: What remains from 1400 mm after 400 mm storage?
quiz.explanation: The remainder is 1000 mm; actual use still needs review.

assignment.prompt: Submit desk/storage drawings, opening states, the exercise calculation and cable routing in two positions with service access.

faq.question: Does hiding cables prove the route is suitable?
faq.answer: No. Review movement, protection, access and system/service requirements.
